Sixty years ago Shastriji Maharaj's suvarna tula mahotsav was celebrated in Atladra by thousands of devotees. They weighed Shastriji Maharaj with sugar crystals. In memory of that landmark celebration a symbolic tula was carried out on that very spot with the utsav murti of Shastriji Maharaj. Swamishri placed sugar crystals on the pan opposite that of Shastriji Maharaj's utsav murti. He also blessed youths and devotees who were dressed as devotees in the time of Shastriji Maharaj.

As part of what has now become a daily ritual, Raghu Bharvad greets Swamishri in a corner of the pradakshina, and lovingly says: "Bapa! Now that I have had your darshan, I feel there is nothing left for me to see or do."

Swamishri humbly acknowledged Raghu's sentiments, and then remarked: "In the time of Shriji Maharaj, there was Jodho Bharvad [of Gadhada]. Here [in Sarangpur], there was Hajo Bharvad. Now, we have you!"

Suresh is an exuberant youth from Botad. He descends from a devout and dedicated family that has served most sincerely since the times of Shastriji Maharaj.

Today, Suresh is holding a tamburo - a single-stringed musical instrument. As Swamishri comes, he starts plucking away and mumbling 'Swaminarayan' Swaminarayan'' He then offers the tamburo to Swamishri, gesturing him to do the same. Swamishri complies graciously, and begins to pluck the instrument and chant 'Swaminarayan' Swaminarayan''
On his way out of the Rang Mandap, Swamishri sees Suresh seated with the tamburo, and smilingly acknowledges this simple youth's devotion.

As part of what has now become a daily ritual, Raghu Bharvad greets Swamishri in a corner of the pradakshina, and lovingly says: "Bapa! Now that I have had your darshan, I feel there is nothing left for me to see or do."

Swamishri humbly acknowledged Raghu's sentiments, and then remarked: "In the time of Shriji Maharaj, there was Jodho Bharvad [of Gadhada]. Here [in Sarangpur], there was Hajo Bharvad. Now, we have you!"

Suresh is an exuberant youth from Botad. He descends from a devout and dedicated family that has served most sincerely since the times of Shastriji Maharaj.

Today, Suresh is holding a tamburo - a single-stringed musical instrument. As Swamishri comes, he starts plucking away and mumbling 'Swaminarayan' Swaminarayan'' He then offers the tamburo to Swamishri, gesturing him to do the same. Swamishri complies graciously, and begins to pluck the instrument and chant 'Swaminarayan' Swaminarayan''
On his way out of the Rang Mandap, Swamishri sees Suresh seated with the tamburo, and smilingly acknowledges this simple youth's devotion.

As part of what has now become a daily ritual, Raghu Bharvad greets Swamishri in a corner of the pradakshina, and lovingly says: "Bapa! Now that I have had your darshan, I feel there is nothing left for me to see or do."

Swamishri humbly acknowledged Raghu's sentiments, and then remarked: "In the time of Shriji Maharaj, there was Jodho Bharvad [of Gadhada]. Here [in Sarangpur], there was Hajo Bharvad. Now, we have you!"

Suresh is an exuberant youth from Botad. He descends from a devout and dedicated family that has served most sincerely since the times of Shastriji Maharaj.

Today, Suresh is holding a tamburo - a single-stringed musical instrument. As Swamishri comes, he starts plucking away and mumbling 'Swaminarayan' Swaminarayan'' He then offers the tamburo to Swamishri, gesturing him to do the same. Swamishri complies graciously, and begins to pluck the instrument and chant 'Swaminarayan' Swaminarayan''
On his way out of the Rang Mandap, Swamishri sees Suresh seated with the tamburo, and smilingly acknowledges this simple youth's devotion.

As part of what has now become a daily ritual, Raghu Bharvad greets Swamishri in a corner of the pradakshina, and lovingly says: "Bapa! Now that I have had your darshan, I feel there is nothing left for me to see or do."

Swamishri humbly acknowledged Raghu's sentiments, and then remarked: "In the time of Shriji Maharaj, there was Jodho Bharvad [of Gadhada]. Here [in Sarangpur], there was Hajo Bharvad. Now, we have you!"

Suresh is an exuberant youth from Botad. He descends from a devout and dedicated family that has served most sincerely since the times of Shastriji Maharaj.

Today, Suresh is holding a tamburo - a single-stringed musical instrument. As Swamishri comes, he starts plucking away and mumbling 'Swaminarayan' Swaminarayan'' He then offers the tamburo to Swamishri, gesturing him to do the same. Swamishri complies graciously, and begins to pluck the instrument and chant 'Swaminarayan' Swaminarayan''
On his way out of the Rang Mandap, Swamishri sees Suresh seated with the tamburo, and smilingly acknowledges this simple youth's devotion.

During the journey to London Mandir, Swamishri observes an origami swan and other shapes as he is informed of their symbolism during the devotional welcome awaiting him at London Mandir

BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Neasden, London – popularly called ‘London Mandir’ and ‘Neasden Temple’ Mahant Swami Maharaj had described London Mandir as “Our Home” during the Mandir’s 25th anniversary in 2020; a large sign bearing his handwritten message was ready to welcome him
Thousands of devotees and hundreds of volunteers had started arriving at London Mandir from as early as 3.30am in eager anticipation of Swamishri's arrival
As the van turned into Pramukh Swami Road, volunteers offered their dandvats to Thakorji and Swamishri

Swamishri’s path throughout the Mandir had been flanked by various origami (artistically folded paper) shapes symbolising various aspects of ‘The Divyabhav Project’ and ‘The Antardrashti Project’ that he had advised would be the best way to prepare for his visitTo learn more about this unique devotional welcome, please click here
Origami swans, symbolising purity and discretion, decorated the bannisters around Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj
Swamishri performing abhishek of Shri Nilkanth Varni
Swamishri entering the upper sanctum of the Mandir

The four types of origami shapes – clams, butterflies, swans, and lotuses – depicted devotees’ pledges of seeing virtues in others, an inner transformation from seeing divinity in others, humility and service, and remaining pure amidst impurities; more than 5,500 of these shapes had been patiently hand-folded by the devotees

All nearby car parks are full as haribhaktas flock to the Mandir for Mahant Swami Maharaj's darshan
Swamishri emerges from his room at 5.20am to make his way to the abhishek mandap
On his way, he stops and stoops to offer a flower to the mahapuja in progress
5.24am: Swamishri performs abhishek of Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj
Swamishri performs the morning arti of the central shrine murtis at 5.33am
Swamishri begins a ceremonial procession of the Swaminarayan-Siddhant-Sudha vaad-granth from the upper sanctum...
Swamishri to the assembly hall, amid jubilation with flags, dancing and celebratory music
Swamishri inaugurates the all-day 'Akshar-Purushottam Darshan Chhavani' by lighting the divo
Swamishri performs the pujan of Swaminarayan-Siddhant-Sudha, authored by Mahamahopadhyaya Bhadreshdas Swami
5.47am: Swamishri commences his morning puja
Swaminarayan-Siddhant-Sudha is a classical Sanskrit treatise that provides a systematic exposition, justification and defence of Akshar-Purushottam Darshan
5.50am: Swamishri is chanting the 'Swaminarayan' mahamantra with his mala
Swamis sing bhajans extolling Akshar-Purushottam Darshan and Shastriji Maharaj
6.04am: Swamishri's chanting with the mala continues
Hundreds of devotees have filled the assembly hall...
Swamishri arriving early to secure a seat...
Swamishri eager to catch closer darshan of Swamishri
Others are sat in the adjacent gymnasium...
Swamishri while yet more watch on a large screen in the overflow marquee in the mandir grounds
6.16: Swamishri stands to perform his tapni mala
6.18am: Swamishri begins his pradakshinas
Swamishri completes six pradakshinas in total
6.21: Swamishri offers thal to Harikrishna Maharaj and the other murtis
6.27: Swamishri sanctifies water with the holy relics of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the Guru Parampara
6.30am: Swamishri concludes his puja by reading the Shikshapatri
6.34: As he completes his puja, Swamishri greets everyone with folded hands
The devotees reciprocate with folded hands
6.39: Swamishri's hands are still folded
Children also fold their hands in return
Swamishri asks for the children to stand and come closer so he can greet them properly
Swamishri rings the bell in honour of the resounding propagation of Akshar-Purushottam Darshan by Shastriji Maharaj, thus commencing the day's learning
Swamishri begins the chhavani by addressing the assembly himself
Swamishri blesses the forthcoming English translation of Likhitan Shastri Yagnapurushdas, produced by BAPS yuvatis in the UK
Ishwarcharandas Swami introduces another forthcoming English publication, Mahant Swami Maharaj: Episodes and Incidents from Yogiji Maharaj's Biography
In keeping with chhavani custom, haribhaktas were to enjoy 'Swaminarayan khichdi' for lunch
Swamishri helped prepare the khichdi in the morning, as mahaprasad for all the attendees
Swamishri also prepared khichdi for Thakorji...
Swamishri expertly adding all the ingredients in turn
Swamishri soon returned to the assembly hall, at 9am...
Swamishri listening attentively to the discourses by various learned swamis
At one point, Swamishri asked for the microphone, sharing his own reflections upon the on-going discourses
As devotees reconvened at 4pm, after lunch and a short break, Swamishri joined the discourses again...
Swamishri continuing to listen to the discourses on Akshar-Purushottam Darshan
In his concluding address, Swamishri read out a pledge to Akshar-Purushottam Darshan
Swamishri had spent a total of more than seven hours in the chhavani, and spoken four times
Swamishri concluded the chhavani with the arti of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj
